pairs.question: What if I prefer to speak to someone in a language other than English?
pairs.answer: Most quitlines can arrange for a translator if you or someone you know who wants to quit speaks a different language. It's great that you're considering reaching out for help!
pairs.evidence: Most quitlines can arrange for a translator if you or someone you know who wants to quit speaks a different language.

pairs.question: Will they make me feel bad about smoking?
pairs.answer: Absolutely not! Quitline coaches are hired and trained based on their ability to help you. They understand what you are going through because many used to smoke themselves.
pairs.evidence: Absolutely not! Quitline coaches are hired and trained based on their ability to help you. Many used to smoke themselves, so they understand what you are going through.

pairs.question: Can Quitline help me if I use other tobacco products?
pairs.answer: Yes, Quitline coaches can help you if you are using smokeless tobacco, cigars, hookah, e-cigarettes, or other tobacco products, in addition to cigarettes. You're not alone in this journey!
pairs.evidence: Quitline coaches can help you if you are using smokeless tobacco, cigars, hookah, e-cigarettes, or other tobacco products, in addition to cigarettes.

pairs.question: What if I want to help a friend who smokes?
pairs.answer: It can be tough to help a friend or family member who smokes. Quit coaches can help you come up with a plan to help them quit, even if they don’t want to quit right now.
pairs.evidence: Quit coaches can help you come up with a plan to help them quit.

pairs.question: How do I know if using a quitline will help me?
pairs.answer: Many studies over the past 25 years show that people who call a quitline are more likely to quit and stay quit. Combining counseling and quit-smoking medications such as patches can double or triple your chances of success.
pairs.evidence: Many studies have been done over the past 25 years on the advantages of quitlines. These studies report that people who call a quitline are more likely to quit and stay quit. Combining counseling and quit-smoking medications such as patches can double or triple your chances of success.

pairs.question: What if I don’t like talking on the phone?
pairs.answer: There are other ways to quit! Quitlines can help you find out about other quit-smoking services, such as apps and texting programs. You have options!
pairs.evidence: Quitlines can help you find out about other quit-smoking services, such as apps and texting programs.

pairs.question: Is calling a quitline free?
pairs.answer: Yes, quitline services are free to callers. It's a great resource to help you quit smoking without any cost.
pairs.evidence: No. Quitline services are free to callers.

pairs.question: What kind of information will they ask me about my smoking?
pairs.answer: They will ask about your smoking status and history, as well as past attempts at quitting and what caused you to continue smoking. This helps them provide better support for you.

pairs.question: What if I don't want to answer a question?
pairs.answer: If you do not feel comfortable answering a question, you can always choose not to answer. Your comfort is important during the process.
pairs.evidence: If you do not feel comfortable answering a question, you can always choose not to answer.

pairs.question: Will they ask about my age, sex, and race?
pairs.answer: Yes, you may also be asked your age, sex, and race. This information helps them tailor their support to your needs.
pairs.evidence: You may also be asked your age, sex, and race.

pairs.question: What happens after I call the quitline?
pairs.answer: After your initial call, you may receive follow-up coaching to support your quitting journey. They want to help you succeed.
